Universal theorem follows from exact 3-party ballot decomposition and discrete concavity, not the finite check.
correctness.rationale: For three parties, partition nonempty approval ballots by singleton i, complement-of-i, and all-three. With K seats, score is cH_K+sum_i(a_i H_{k_i}+b_i H_{K-k_i}). Forward marginal delta_i(t)=a_i/(t+1)-b_i/(K-t) is nonincreasing. One-seat-exchange local optimality forces every last selected marginal >= every first unselected marginal in other party; monotonicity extends inequality to all selected vs unselected entries including same party. Thus selected K marginals are global top K; greedy prefix selection is optimal. m=1,2 similarly. The m=4 K=2 obstruction was published previously and is not claimed new.
residual_risks: Finite independent checks verify stated finite claims only; all-parameter conclusions depend on reconstructed mathematical arguments.
